mainEntity.name: How much does a tax return cost in Australia?

acceptedAnswer.text: A simple individual return typically costs $200–$400. Add a rental property ($350–$550), a CGT event ($300–$800) or trust distributions ($600–$1,200). The matched agent quotes after reviewing your situation — the matching is free.

mainEntity.name: How much does a bookkeeper cost per month?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most small businesses spend $400–$1,200 per month for ongoing bookkeeping, though catch-up work or payroll-heavy businesses can be more. BAS-only engagements are usually $250-$400 per quarter. The matched bookkeeper gives you a clear quote.

mainEntity.name: How much does an SMSF accountant cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Annual SMSF accounting and audit typically ranges from $1,500 to $3,500 depending on complexity — more if the fund holds property or has borrowings. The matched specialist gives you a clear quote after reviewing your fund.
Yes. Your Accountant Match is free for individuals and businesses. We are engaged by the accounting firms in our network, not by you. You are under no obligation to proceed with any matched firm.

mainEntity.name: How much does a company tax return cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A company or trust tax return typically costs $500–$1,500 depending on entity count, complexity and the state of the books. Ongoing accounting is usually $400–$1,000 per month. The matched accountant gives you a clear quote — the matching is free.

mainEntity.name: How much does a small business accountant cost per month?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most small businesses spend $400–$1,000 per month for ongoing accounting and compliance. Project work like structuring or forecasting is quoted separately. The matched firm gives you a clear quote after reviewing your situation.

mainEntity.name: Does a more expensive accountant mean a better result?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The right match is about finding a firm whose expertise fits your needs — not over-buying credentials. A straightforward return does not need a CPA-signed audit report. Matching to the right credential keeps costs down while ensuring the work is done correctly.

mainEntity.name: How quickly will a matched accountant contact me?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most matches are completed within 60 seconds of finishing the questionnaire. Your matched firm will typically reach out within 2 hours, or you can call for immediate assistance to discuss your needs and get a quote.

VB WRITTEN BY Vic Bulfone Founder, Your Accountant Match LAST REVIEWED 29 September 2026 Last verified against ATO guidance 29 September 2026 PRICING GUIDE Understanding Accountant Costs in Australia Individual tax return costs A straightforward individual return (one employer, no investments) typically costs $200–$400. Complexity pushes the price up: a rental property adds depreciation-schedule work ($350–$550), a CGT event from selling shares or property adds $300–$800, and trust distributions or foreign income can take a return to $600–$1,200. The matched agent quotes after reviewing your situation — the matching itself is free. Business accounting & BAS costs Ongoing small-business accounting typically runs $400–$1,000 per month for compliance. BAS preparation alone is usually $250–$400 per quarter depending on transaction volume. Catch-up work (overdue BAS or multiple years behind) is quoted separately and can be higher. Payroll-heavy businesses and those with inventory tend toward the top of the range. SMSF & specialist costs Annual SMSF accounting and audit typically ranges from $1,500 to $3,500 — more if the fund holds property, has borrowings (LRBA) or needs Division 296 modelling. Specialist work like audit & assurance, business valuation or growth advisory is usually quoted as a fixed fee or monthly retainer ($500–$3,000+/month for advisory). What drives the price — and how to control it Three things move the price: complexity (entities, investments, structures), the state of your records (clean books cost less to process), and the credential required (a CPA-signed audit report costs more than a routine return). The biggest lever you control is record-keeping — tidy, reconciled books mean a faster, cheaper engagement. Matching to the right credential (not over-buying) is the second.
